Name: Approvals page renders header, filter bar and table columns
Objective: Verify the User Approvals page shows the correct header/subtitle, the four status filter buttons, the date-range filter, the pending-count badge, and all seven table columns.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one pending registration exists in the current tenant.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals.
2. Observe the PageHeader title 'User Approvals' and its subtitle.
3. Observe the Status filter row with buttons Pending, Approved, Rejected, All and the date-range (from/to) inputs.
4. Inspect the amber count pill on the Pending button.
5. Inspect the table header row and one pending data row.
ExpectedResult: Header title is 'User Approvals'. With pending rows present the subtitle reads 'N registration(s) awaiting approval' (singular 'registration' when exactly 1). The Pending button is highlighted by default and carries an amber pill showing the pending count. Table columns are Applicant (name + email), Company, Contact, GSTIN, Requested, Status, Actions (right-aligned). Empty fields render as '—'. Footer reads 'Only the super admin can see and action this page.'

Name: Status badge tone and conditional action buttons per status
Objective: Verify each user's Status badge uses the correct tone and that Approve/Reject buttons are shown or hidden according to the user's current status.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; the tenant has one pending, one approved and one rejected user (use the All filter to see all three).
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals and click the All filter.
2. Locate the pending, approved and rejected rows.
3. Inspect the Status badge colour/text on each.
4. Inspect the Actions cell on each row.
ExpectedResult: Status badges: pending = amber, approved = green, rejected = red, each showing the raw status word. Pending row shows BOTH Approve (primary, Check icon) and Reject (red secondary, X icon). Approved row shows ONLY Reject (Approve hidden). Rejected row shows ONLY Approve (Reject hidden).

Name: Rows sorted newest-first by requested date
Objective: Verify the pending list is ordered by createdAt descending (most recent registration at the top).
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least two pending registrations with distinct createdAt values exist.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals (Pending filter is active by default).
2. Read the Requested column top-to-bottom.
ExpectedResult: Rows are sorted by Requested date descending — the newest sign-up appears first. Rows missing a createdAt sort to the bottom and still display '—' in the Requested column without breaking the order.

Name: Reject requires explicit confirmation dialog
Objective: Verify clicking Reject opens a danger confirmation dialog with the correct copy and that cancelling makes no change.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one non-rejected user is listed.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals.
2. Click Reject on a pending or approved user.
3. Read the confirmation dialog title, message and buttons.
4. Click Cancel (dismiss without confirming).
5. Observe the user's status.
ExpectedResult: A confirm dialog appears with title 'Reject registration', message 'Reject {name or email}? They will not be able to sign in.', a danger-styled 'Reject' confirm button and a Cancel button. Cancelling closes the dialog and leaves the user's status unchanged (no toast, no data write).

Name: Date-range filter includes and excludes by requested date
Objective: Verify the from/to date-range filter inclusively bounds rows by createdAt and that empty bounds mean unbounded.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least two users with createdAt dates on different days exist.
TestData: from = the earlier user's date; to = same earlier date
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals and select the All filter.
2. Note the Requested dates of the visible users.
3. Set the 'from' and 'to' dates to bracket only the earlier user's date.
4. Clear both date fields.
ExpectedResult: With a bracketing range only users whose createdAt falls inside the inclusive range remain; users outside the range disappear. Users lacking a createdAt are excluded whenever a 'from' is set (empty date fails the lower bound). Clearing both dates restores the full list (unbounded).

Name: All four status filters plus empty-state copy per filter
Objective: Verify each status filter (Pending / Approved / Rejected / All) narrows the list to the matching status, the date-range filter composes with it, and the correct empty-state copy shows per filter.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin. Ideally have at least one user in each status; for the empty-state checks use a tenant/filter combination that yields zero rows.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals; confirm Pending is the default active filter.
2. Click Approved, then Rejected, then All, inspecting the Status column each time.
3. With All selected, apply a date range that matches no user and observe the empty state.
4. Switch to Pending on a tenant/date-range that yields no pending rows and read the empty-state title and description.
5. Switch to Approved (or Rejected/All) on a filter that yields no rows and read the empty-state title and description.
ExpectedResult: Pending shows only pending users, Approved only approved, Rejected only rejected, All shows every user regardless of status. The date-range filter further narrows any selection. When no rows match: the Pending filter shows title 'No pending registrations' with description 'New sign-ups will appear here for your approval.'; every other filter shows title 'No records' with description 'Nothing to show for this filter.'

Name: Approve a pending registration
Objective: Verify approving a pending user updates status to approved, shows a success toast, refreshes the list, and hides the Approve button.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; a disposable pending registration exists (create one via /signup if needed).
TestData: Pending applicant with a known fullName/email
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals (Pending filter).
2. Click Approve on the target pending user.
3. Observe the toast.
4. Observe the row after the list refreshes (it drops off the Pending filter); switch to Approved to confirm.
5. Inspect the Actions cell for the now-approved user.
ExpectedResult: A success toast '{fullName or email} approved' appears. The users query is invalidated and refetched: the user's status becomes 'approved' (green badge under Approved/All), it no longer appears under Pending, the pending count decreases, and the Approve button is hidden for that user (only Reject remains).

Name: Reject a registration after confirming
Objective: Verify confirming the Reject dialog sets status to rejected, shows a success toast, refreshes the list, and hides the Reject button.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; a disposable pending (or approved) registration exists.
TestData: Disposable applicant
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals.
2. Click Reject on the target user and confirm 'Reject' in the dialog.
3. Observe the toast.
4. Switch to the Rejected filter and locate the user.
5. Inspect the Actions cell for the rejected user.
ExpectedResult: Success toast 'Registration rejected' appears. The list refreshes and the user's status becomes 'rejected' (red badge under Rejected/All). The Reject button is hidden for that user (only Approve remains).

Name: Approved/All filters render without a client crash when a user lacks a created date
Objective: Regression: verify switching to the Approved and All filters renders the table without a client-side crash even when a listed user (e.g. a legacy/seed account or the super admin) has no createdAt.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin. The users list includes at least one account with no createdAt (the super-admin/legacy seed account qualifies) — visible under Approved and/or All.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals.
2. Click the Approved filter and wait for the table to render.
3. Click the All filter and wait for the table to render.
4. Open the browser console / inspect the DOM root.
5. Confirm the created-date-less user appears with '—' in the Requested column.
ExpectedResult: Both the Approved and All views render normally — the page does NOT crash: no '<html id="__next_error__">', no 'This page couldn't load' error screen, no console error from calling .slice on undefined. Users without a createdAt display '—' in the Requested column and sort to the bottom. (Guarded by (u.createdAt ?? '') in the inRange filter and sort comparator.)

Name: Approve/Reject mirror decision to set_user_approval and refresh cache
Objective: Verify an approve/reject writes app_state via upsert and issues the set_user_approval RPC, and that the users query is invalidated so the UI reflects the new state.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin with browser DevTools Network tab open; a disposable pending user exists.
Steps:
1. Open DevTools > Network and filter to Supabase REST/RPC calls.
2. Navigate to /app/approvals and Approve the disposable user.
3. Inspect the network calls made during the action.
4. Observe whether the users list refetches.
ExpectedResult: An upsert to the app_state table (id 'singleton') persists the users array with the user's status='approved', decidedAt (ISO timestamp) and decidedBy set. An RPC POST to set_user_approval with { p_email, p_approved: true } is sent (a 'function does not exist' error is silently ignored; any other RPC error surfaces an error toast). After success the qk.users.all query is invalidated and refetched, updating the table without a manual reload.

Name: Approve/Reject failure surfaces an error toast
Objective: Verify a failed approve/reject mutation shows the correct fallback error toast and does not falsely report success.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; ability to force a backend failure (e.g. block the app_state upsert / set_user_approval RPC via DevTools request blocking, or go offline).
Steps:
1. Open DevTools and block the Supabase app_state upsert (or the set_user_approval RPC) request, or disable the network.
2. Navigate to /app/approvals and click Approve on a user.
3. Repeat with Reject (confirm the dialog first).
4. Observe the toast and the row status.
ExpectedResult: Approve failure shows an error toast defaulting to 'Approve failed' (or the mapped server message via toUserMessage); Reject failure shows 'Reject failed'. No success toast appears and the user's displayed status is unchanged.

Name: Non-super-admin is redirected away from /app/approvals
Objective: Verify a regular approved (non-super-admin) user cannot view the approvals page and is redirected to /app.
Precondition: Logged in as a regular approved User (NOT a SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS account).
TestData: Regular user session
Steps:
1. While logged in as a regular user, navigate directly to /app/approvals.
2. Observe the resulting page/route.
ExpectedResult: The approvals content never renders (component returns null) and the app navigates (replace) to /app. No user list, filters or action buttons are shown to the non-super-admin.

Name: Unauthenticated access to /app/approvals is blocked by the shell
Objective: Verify an unauthenticated visitor cannot reach the approvals page and is redirected to the public landing by the portal shell.
Precondition: No active session (logged out / fresh browser).
Steps:
1. Ensure you are logged out.
2. Navigate directly to /app/approvals.
3. Observe the redirect target.
ExpectedResult: The authenticated portal shell (app/app/layout.tsx) redirects to '/' (not /login). No approvals data is exposed to an unauthenticated request.

Name: Super-admin identity limited to SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS
Objective: Verify only accounts whose email is in SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS are treated as super admin and can see/action approvals.
Precondition: Access to both a SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS account (QA super-admin) and a regular approved account.
TestData: Super-admin email vs. a non-listed email
Steps:
1. Log in as the QA super-admin (email in SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS) and open /app/approvals.
2. Log out and log in as a regular approved user, then open /app/approvals.
ExpectedResult: The SUPER_ADMIN_EMAILS account sees the full approvals page (session.role SuperAdmin, isSuperAdmin true). The non-listed account is treated as a regular User (isSuperAdmin false) and is redirected to /app with no access. Email matching is case-insensitive.

Name: Approval decision persists in app_state.data.users
Objective: Verify approve/reject decisions persist to app_state.data.users (status, decidedAt, decidedBy) and survive a page reload.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; a disposable pending user exists.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/approvals and Approve the disposable user.
2. Hard-reload the page (or re-open /app/approvals).
3. Switch to the Approved filter and confirm the user's state.
4. (Optional) Inspect app_state.data.users in Supabase to confirm the stored fields.
ExpectedResult: After reload the user is still status 'approved' under the Approved filter. The persisted record carries status='approved', a decidedAt ISO timestamp and decidedBy = the super-admin username (falling back to 'admin'). The decision is not lost on refresh (written to the singleton app_state row, not just client state).

Name: Approval decision gates downstream login
Objective: Verify the persisted status is enforced at login — pending cannot sign in, rejected is refused, approved can sign in.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; access to a disposable applicant's credentials (created via /signup).
TestData: Disposable applicant email/password
Steps:
1. As super-admin, leave the applicant pending; attempt to log in as that applicant.
2. As super-admin, Reject the applicant; attempt to log in again.
3. As super-admin, Approve the applicant; attempt to log in again.
ExpectedResult: Pending login is blocked with 'Your account is awaiting super-admin approval.'; rejected login is refused with 'Your registration was not approved. Please contact the administrator.'; approved login succeeds and reaches /app. This confirms the approvals decision (mirrored to set_user_approval and reflected by resolveSupabaseSession) drives access.

Name: Dashboard renders all sections with header, scope subtitle and company filter
Objective: Verify the /app dashboard loads and displays the page header, today's date + scope label, company filter, workflow stepper, all panel cards, charts and lists.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; account has seeded jobs, invoices, payments, expenses, materials and companies.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app.
2. Observe the PageHeader title 'Dashboard' and subtitle.
3. Confirm the subtitle shows today's date (formatted via fmtDate) followed by ' · All companies'.
4. Confirm the company filter <Select> (aria-label 'Filter dashboard by company') is present with 'All companies' selected.
5. Scroll and confirm the WorkflowStepper (5 stages), Shop-floor activity, Financial summary, Job orders by status, Stock health, Purchase & raw material panels, all four charts, and the four lists render.
ExpectedResult: The dashboard renders fully with no crash (the live DOM does not contain <html id="__next_error__">); header, subtitle scoped to 'All companies', company filter, stepper, panels, charts and lists are all visible.

Name: Workflow stepper, KPI tiles, summary rows and 'View all' links navigate to correct routes
Objective: Verify each WorkflowStepper stage, BigStat tile, financial SummaryRow and list 'View all' link navigates via AppLink to its documented route without a full-page error.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin.
Steps:
1. On /app, click the 'Material Stock' stepper stage -> /app/inventory/materials, then go back.
2. Click 'Job Orders' -> /app/jobs; 'In Machining' -> /app/production; 'Ready to Dispatch' -> /app/production; 'Dispatched' -> /app/deliveries, returning to /app each time.
3. Click the 'Open Jobs' BigStat -> /app/jobs and the 'Dispatched' BigStat -> /app/deliveries.
4. Click the Financial summary 'Payments (month)' row -> /app/payments and 'Pending payments' row -> /app/invoices.
5. Click 'View all' on Recent payments -> /app/payments and on Recent material dispatches -> /app/inventory/materials (note: NOT /app/deliveries).
ExpectedResult: Every linked element navigates to its documented route (stepper/BigStat/SummaryRow/View-all targets above) without a full page error; the app shell remains intact after each navigation.

Name: Empty-state messages render for charts and lists that have no in-scope data
Objective: Verify empty states for the expenses pie, dispatched bar and the four lists when there is no data in scope, and that the two 6-month money bar charts still render (they have no empty state).
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; select a company (or use a scope) that has no expenses this month, no material issues, no pending jobs and no payments.
TestData: Company with no current-month/recent activity.
Steps:
1. On /app, choose a company from the filter that has no in-scope activity.
2. Inspect 'Expenses by category (month)' and 'Materials dispatched per month'.
3. Inspect the Priority jobs, Low/negative stock, Recent payments and Recent material dispatches lists.
4. Inspect 'Invoices raised vs Payments received (6 months)' and 'Cash flow: Payments vs Expenses (6 months)'.
ExpectedResult: Expenses pie shows 'No expenses this month'; dispatched bar shows 'No material issues in this period'; lists show 'No pending jobs', 'All stock above reorder levels', 'No payments yet' and 'No material issues yet' respectively. The two 6-month money bar charts render their axes/legends with zero-height bars (they have no empty-state text).

Name: Charts render bars, pie, legends, tooltips and the stock-health gauge percentage
Objective: Verify recharts visuals render correctly and the Stock health donut shows the centered whole-number percentage with 'in stock' caption.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin with seeded invoices, payments, expenses and material issues across recent months.
Steps:
1. On /app, hover a bar in 'Invoices raised vs Payments received (6 months)' and confirm a currency-formatted tooltip and the Invoiced/Received legend.
2. Hover 'Cash flow: Payments vs Expenses (6 months)' and confirm the Payments/Expenses legend and currency-formatted tooltip.
3. Hover 'Materials dispatched per month' and confirm the tooltip shows a quantity (qty format, not currency) and there is no legend/second series.
4. Confirm the Stock health donut shows a whole-number percentage in the center with the 'in stock' caption.
ExpectedResult: All charts render with correct axes/legends; tooltips use currency for the money charts and qty for the dispatched chart; the gauge shows the computed healthy-stock percentage as a whole number.

Name: Company filter re-scopes every KPI, chart and list
Objective: Verify selecting a company filters jobs/invoices/payments/expenses/issues and re-computes all figures (including company-scoped stock balances) for that company only.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least two companies exist with distinct jobs, invoices, payments, expenses and material data.
TestData: Company A and Company B with known, differing figures.
Steps:
1. On /app with 'All companies', note Open Jobs, Invoiced (month), Pending payments, Raw material value and the Priority jobs / Recent payments lists.
2. Select Company A in the filter.
3. Confirm the subtitle scope label changes to Company A's name.
4. Confirm KPI tiles, financial summary, job-status counts, stock health, charts and all four lists now reflect only Company A's data.
5. Switch to 'All companies' and confirm figures revert to the aggregate.
ExpectedResult: All KPIs, charts and lists recompute to the selected company's scope; subtitle updates to the company name; clearing the filter restores the aggregate view. Note: stock panels iterate the full materials list but re-derive each balance in company scope, so materials with no company-scoped movement show balance 0 (counted as 'Out of stock' in the gauge) and Raw material value uses companyMaterialValue.

Name: Monthly financial figures, Net(month) tone, and Cancelled/all-time exclusions are correct
Objective: Verify Invoiced/GST/Payments/Expenses (month) reflect only current-calendar-month records, Cancelled invoices are excluded, Net(month)=payments-expenses with red tone when negative, and 'Pending payments' is all-time (not month-scoped).
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; seeded invoices in the current month and prior months (incl. at least one Cancelled this month), plus payments and expenses this month and in prior months.
TestData: Invoices dated this month (mix of statuses incl. Cancelled) and last month; payments and expenses this month and prior; a scope where this-month expenses exceed this-month payments.
Steps:
1. On /app, read Invoiced (month), GST (month), Payments (month), Expenses (month) and Net (month).
2. Compare against the sum of only current-month, non-Cancelled invoice totals/tax (via computeInvoice) and current-month payments/expenses.
3. Confirm a Cancelled invoice dated this month adds nothing to Invoiced, GST or Pending payments.
4. Confirm prior-month invoices/payments/expenses do not contribute to the (month) figures, but DO contribute to 'Pending payments' if outstanding (pending is all-time over non-Cancelled invoices).
5. For the negative scope, confirm Net (month) equals payments-expenses and is shown with the red tone (green when non-negative).
ExpectedResult: Monthly figures equal the current-month totals derived by computeInvoice; Cancelled invoices contribute nothing to invoiced/GST/pending; prior-month records are excluded from the (month) figures; Pending payments is the all-time outstanding over non-Cancelled in-scope invoices; Net(month)=payments-expenses with red tone when negative and green otherwise.

Name: Job-status counts, workflow stepper and priority-jobs ordering are consistent
Objective: Verify job counts (Open, In Production, Ready, Dispatched, by-status) match job records and Priority jobs are sorted Urgent>High>Normal>Low and limited to 6.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; jobs seeded across statuses Draft/Pending/In Progress/On Hold/Completed/Delivered/Cancelled and priorities Urgent/High/Normal/Low, with more than 6 Pending/In Progress/On Hold jobs.
TestData: Known job set with mixed statuses/priorities (>6 pending-type jobs).
Steps:
1. On /app, note Open Jobs (should equal Pending+Draft), In Production (In Progress), Ready to Dispatch (Completed), Dispatched (Delivered).
2. Cross-check with 'Job orders by status' rows (Pending/In progress/On hold/Completed/Cancelled) and the workflow stepper counts.
3. Inspect the Priority jobs list and confirm it contains only Pending/In Progress/On Hold jobs, is ordered by priority rank (Urgent, High, Normal, Low), and shows at most 6 entries.
ExpectedResult: Open Jobs=Pending+Draft, In Production=In Progress, Ready to Dispatch(stepper)=Completed, Dispatched=Delivered, and by-status rows agree with the underlying records and each other; Priority jobs are correctly filtered to Pending/In Progress/On Hold, priority-ordered and capped at 6.

Name: Stock health gauge, low/negative stock list and raw-material value reflect the stock ledger
Objective: Verify stock balances (received - issued + adjusted) drive the gauge percentage and healthy/low/out classification, the low-stock list, and raw-material value, honoring the exact classification order and the gauge-vs-list filter difference.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; materials seeded to yield at least one healthy (bal>0 and above reorder), one low (reorderLevel set and 0<bal<=reorderLevel), one out (bal<=0), plus one material at exactly bal=0 with no reorderLevel and one with a negative balance.
TestData: Materials with known receipts/issues/adjustments and reorderLevel values (including one with reorderLevel undefined).
Steps:
1. On /app, read the Stock health gauge percentage and the Healthy / Low stock / Out of stock counts.
2. Confirm the classification order: bal<=0 counts as Out first; else (reorderLevel defined and bal<=reorderLevel) counts as Low; else Healthy; and pct = round(healthy/total*100).
3. Inspect the Low/negative stock list; confirm it lists materials with balance<0 OR (reorderLevel defined and balance<=reorderLevel), negative balances shown in red and others amber, capped at 6.
4. Confirm the gauge-vs-list edge: a material at exactly bal=0 with NO reorderLevel is counted as 'Out of stock' in the gauge but does NOT appear in the low-stock list.
5. Confirm Raw material value equals totalRawMaterialValue (or companyMaterialValue when scoped) and 'Materials in stock' equals the count of materials with company-scoped balance>0.
ExpectedResult: Gauge percentage and healthy/low/out counts follow the documented classification order; the low-stock list contents/coloring and the bal=0/no-reorderLevel edge match the code; raw-material value and materials-in-stock count match src/data/computations.ts.

Name: Recent payments and recent material dispatches show latest records first, capped at 5
Objective: Verify the Recent payments and Recent material dispatches lists sort by date descending and are limited to 5, showing correct labels/amounts/units.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; more than 5 payments and more than 5 material issues seeded with varying dates.
TestData: 6+ payments and 6+ issues with known dates.
Steps:
1. On /app, inspect Recent payments; confirm at most 5 rows, newest first, each showing company name (resolved), date, method and currency amount.
2. Inspect Recent material dispatches; confirm at most 5 rows, newest first, each showing material name (resolved), date, issue number and quantity + unit.
ExpectedResult: Both lists show at most 5 entries in descending date order with correctly resolved company/material names and correctly formatted amounts (currency) and quantities (qty + unit).

Name: Dashboard handles empty/absent datasets without errors (default [] guards)
Objective: Verify the read-only screen degrades gracefully when queries return no data — hooks default to [] so no NaN/undefined leaks into KPIs or charts and the gauge guards total=0.
Precondition: Logged in as a QA super-admin on a fresh/empty tenant or an account with no jobs/invoices/payments/expenses/materials.
TestData: Empty dataset.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app with no seeded data.
2. Confirm the page renders without crashing (no <html id="__next_error__">).
3. Confirm numeric count KPIs show 0 and currency KPIs show the zero-value currency format (not NaN/undefined).
4. Confirm the stock-health gauge shows 0% (total=0 guard) and all lists and the empty-capable charts show their empty states.
ExpectedResult: No runtime error; counts render as 0, currency figures are valid zero amounts (no NaN/undefined), the gauge shows 0%, and empty-state text appears for the expenses pie, dispatched bar and all four lists.

Name: Company filter only accepts the provided options
Objective: Verify the company filter is a constrained native <select> whose only values are '' (All companies) and existing company ids, so no arbitrary/invalid scope can be entered.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin with several companies.
Steps:
1. On /app, open the company filter and confirm the first option is 'All companies' (empty value) followed by exactly one option per company.
2. Confirm there is no free-text input for the scope (it is a native <select>).
3. Select each option in turn and confirm the subtitle scope label updates accordingly.
ExpectedResult: The filter exposes only the empty 'All companies' option plus one option per existing company; no invalid/free-form value is possible and the subtitle reflects each selection.

Name: Dashboard issues only read queries to Supabase and does not write
Objective: Verify loading /app triggers the expected read-only data hooks (jobs, invoices, payments, expenses, issues, materials, companies, receipts, adjustments) and performs no mutating requests or RPC writes, and that changing the filter does not fetch.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; browser DevTools/Network panel available.
Steps:
1. Open DevTools Network, clear it, then navigate to /app.
2. Confirm read requests for jobs, invoices, payments, expenses, material issues, materials, companies, receipts and adjustments are issued (GET/select).
3. Confirm there are no POST/PATCH/DELETE table writes and no create_/transition_ RPC calls triggered by the dashboard.
4. Change the company filter and confirm no new network requests occur (filtering is client-side over cached data).
ExpectedResult: Only read/select requests are made to Supabase; the company filter recomputes client-side with no extra fetches for the cached data; no mutations or write RPCs occur.

Name: Dashboard tolerates a failing query and does not render a client-side crash page
Objective: Verify the dashboard tolerates a failing/slow query (hook data falls back to []) and does not render a client-side crash page.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; ability to simulate a failed request (e.g. block one Supabase endpoint in DevTools).
Steps:
1. Open DevTools and block/force-fail one of the dashboard endpoints (e.g. expenses).
2. Navigate to /app.
3. Observe rendering of the sections that depend on the failed endpoint (e.g. Expenses(month), expenses pie, cash flow, Net).
4. Confirm the live DOM does not contain <html id="__next_error__">.
ExpectedResult: The dashboard still renders; sections backed by the failed query fall back to empty/zero states rather than crashing the whole page.

Name: Dashboard route requires authentication
Objective: Verify /app is gated by the app-shell auth layout and unauthenticated users cannot view dashboard data.
Precondition: No active session (logged out / fresh browser).
Steps:
1. Clear the session and navigate directly to /app.
2. Observe the app-shell auth gate behavior (redirect/block).
3. Confirm no dashboard KPIs, charts or lists (customer/financial data) are rendered while unauthenticated.
ExpectedResult: Unauthenticated access to /app is blocked/redirected by the auth gate; no dashboard data is exposed before authentication.

Name: Dashboard data is tenant/RLS scoped to the signed-in account
Objective: Verify the dashboard only aggregates data the authenticated user is entitled to (RLS/tenant isolation), so no other tenant's companies, jobs, invoices or payments appear.
Precondition: Two isolated accounts/tenants exist, each with distinct data.
TestData: Tenant A and Tenant B with known, non-overlapping records.
Steps:
1. Log in as Tenant A and record the dashboard figures and company filter options.
2. Log out and log in as Tenant B.
3. Compare the dashboard figures and company filter list.
4. Confirm Tenant B never sees Tenant A's companies, jobs, invoices or payment totals.
ExpectedResult: Each account's dashboard reflects only its own data; the company filter lists only that account's companies; no cross-tenant leakage occurs (enforced by Supabase RLS).

Name: Dashboard money/stock figures are derived, not denormalised — recompute after underlying data changes
Objective: Verify dashboard aggregates are computed from authoritative rows (invoices, payments, issues, receipts, adjustments) so they update correctly when source data changes, with no stale denormalised value.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; able to add a payment and a material issue through their own modules (test/staging data).
TestData: One new payment (current month, allocated to an outstanding invoice) and one new material issue in a chosen company scope.
Steps:
1. On /app, note Payments (month), Pending payments, the Materials dispatched chart and Recent material dispatches for a company scope.
2. In the Payments module, record a new current-month payment allocated to an outstanding invoice for that company; return to /app (refresh/invalidate).
3. Confirm Payments (month) increases by the payment amount and Pending payments decreases by the allocated amount (via computeInvoice outstanding).
4. In the Materials module, record a new issue for that company; return to /app and confirm the dispatched chart bucket and Recent dispatches reflect it.
ExpectedResult: Dashboard figures recompute from the updated ledger (payments/outstanding and dispatched quantities change to match) with no stale cached/denormalised values. Destructive because it writes payment/issue rows in other modules to validate derivation.

Name: Invoices list renders summary tiles, GST summary, company-wise table and invoice grid
Objective: Verify the Invoices page renders the header, this-month tiles, GST summary, company-wise summary and the invoice table with all expected columns.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least a few invoices exist across companies.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/invoices.
2. Observe the page header 'Invoices' with Excel and New Invoice actions.
3. Observe the 'This month' section with four StatTiles: Invoices, Invoiced value, Received, Outstanding (each with a vs-last-month delta).
4. Observe the 'GST Summary' four tiles: Taxable value, CGST, SGST, Total GST.
5. Observe the Company-wise summary table with columns Company, Invoices, Total, Paid, Outstanding.
6. Observe the main invoice table columns: Invoice, Date, Company, Total, Paid, Outstanding, Status, Actions.
ExpectedResult: All sections render without errors; tiles show currency-formatted values; the invoice table lists invoices sorted by date descending with a status badge per row.

Name: Row action buttons respect invoice status (Record payment / Edit / Cancel visibility)
Objective: Verify per-row action buttons are shown/hidden based on status: Record payment shows when status is neither Cancelled nor Paid (so Unpaid and Partially Paid both show it), Edit shows when neither Paid nor Cancelled, Cancel shows when not Cancelled, and Download PDF/Print always show.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; invoices exist in Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid and Cancelled statuses.
Steps:
1. Open /app/invoices.
2. Locate an Unpaid invoice row and note its action buttons.
3. Locate a Partially Paid invoice row and note its action buttons.
4. Locate a Paid invoice row and note its action buttons.
5. Locate a Cancelled invoice row and note its action buttons.
ExpectedResult: Unpaid and Partially Paid rows both show Record payment, Download PDF, Print, Edit and Cancel. Paid row hides Record payment and Edit but shows Download PDF, Print and Cancel. Cancelled row shows only Download PDF and Print (Record payment, Edit and Cancel are hidden).

Name: Empty state and filtered empty state display correctly
Objective: Verify the EmptyState and company-summary empty message appear when no invoices match.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin.
TestData: Search term guaranteed to match nothing, e.g. 'zzz-no-match'.
Steps:
1. Open /app/invoices.
2. Type 'zzz-no-match' into the search box.
3. Observe the company-wise summary section and the main invoice card.
ExpectedResult: Company-wise summary shows 'No invoices for the current filters.' and the main card shows the 'No invoices' EmptyState with the create hint ('Create an invoice from completed jobs or manually.').

Name: Live invoice totals recompute correctly from lines, discount, CGST and SGST
Objective: Verify subtotal, taxable, CGST/SGST amounts and total are computed correctly and rounded to two decimals in the form.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; New Invoice modal open.
TestData: Line 1: qty 10, rate 100 (=1000); Line 2: qty 2, rate 250 (=500); Discount 100; CGST 9; SGST 9.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice.
2. Add two line items with the test-data quantities and rates.
3. Enter Discount 100, CGST 9, SGST 9.
4. Read the Subtotal, CGST amount, SGST amount and Total in the totals panel.
ExpectedResult: Subtotal = 1500.00; taxable = 1400; CGST amount = 126.00; SGST amount = 126.00; Total = 1652.00 (all two-decimal rounded). The CGST/SGST amount fields are disabled/read-only.

Name: Discount exceeding subtotal clamps taxable to zero (no negative tax/total)
Objective: Verify taxable value is floored at zero (max(0, subtotal-discount)) when discount exceeds subtotal so tax and total never go negative.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; New Invoice modal open.
TestData: Line: qty 1, rate 500 (=500); Discount 900; CGST 9; SGST 9.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice and add a single line qty 1 rate 500.
2. Enter Discount 900, CGST 9, SGST 9.
3. Read the totals panel.
ExpectedResult: Taxable is treated as 0; CGST amount = 0.00, SGST amount = 0.00, Total = 0.00. No negative values displayed.

Name: Blank invoice number auto-numbers and empty lines are stripped on save
Objective: Verify a blank invoice number falls back to the auto-generated number (nextNumberedDoc) and lines with no description/rate/material are filtered out on submit.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; New Invoice modal open; a company selected and date set.
TestData: One real line (description 'Machining', qty 1, rate 100); one blank line; Invoice Number left empty.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice; select a company and set the invoice date.
2. Fill one line with description 'Machining', qty 1, rate 100.
3. Click Add line to create a second empty line and leave it blank.
4. Leave Invoice Number blank (note the preview placeholder).
5. Click Create invoice.
ExpectedResult: Invoice is created with only the single non-empty line; the invoice number matches the auto-numbering sequence (nextNumberedDoc), not blank.

Name: Changing company drops challan-derived lines and clears the DC reference
Objective: Verify that switching the selected company after importing delivery-challan lines removes those lines, resets the material filter, and clears the Delivery Challan Ref field (lines belong to the prior company).
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; New Invoice modal open; two companies each with at least one Open delivery challan.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice and select Company A.
2. In 'Add from delivery challans', tick one challan so its lines and DC number import.
3. Confirm the imported lines and the auto-filled Delivery Challan Ref.
4. Change the Company selector to Company B.
5. Inspect the line items and the Delivery Challan Ref field.
ExpectedResult: On company change the challan-derived lines are removed, the challan selection and material filter reset, and the Delivery Challan Ref is cleared. Only non-challan lines (if any) remain.

Name: Required Company/Date are not enforced client-side; RPC is the gate
Objective: Verify the form does not hard-block submission when Company or Date is empty (the 'required' markers are advisory); creation is rejected by the create_invoice RPC / backend rather than by a client-side validation message.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; New Invoice modal open; browser dev-tools Network tab open.
TestData: Leave Company as 'Select…' (empty) and Invoice Date empty; add one line 'Test', qty 1, rate 10.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice.
2. Clear/leave the Company as unselected and leave Invoice Date empty.
3. Add a single line item.
4. Click Create invoice and observe whether a client-side validation blocks it before any request, then observe the network request/response.
ExpectedResult: No client-side validation summary blocks the click; the app attempts the create_invoice RPC which rejects the missing company/date (error toast surfaced via toUserMessage). No invalid invoice is persisted. This documents that Company/Date 'required' markers are not enforced locally.

Name: Create a new GST invoice (Unpaid) and verify it appears in the list
Objective: Verify the end-to-end create flow produces an Unpaid invoice with correct totals and it appears in the list and month tiles.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one active company exists.
TestData: Company: any active; Date: today; Line: 'CNC Job', qty 5, rate 200; CGST 9; SGST 9.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice.
2. Select the company, set date to today, add the line item and set CGST 9 / SGST 9.
3. Click Create invoice.
4. Confirm the success toast and locate the new invoice in the list.
ExpectedResult: Invoice is created with status Unpaid, Total = 1180.00, appears at the top of the list (date desc), and the this-month Invoices count / Invoiced value tiles reflect it.

Name: Save invoice as Draft and confirm exclusion from receivables totals
Objective: Verify Save-as-draft creates a Draft invoice and that Draft invoices are excluded from the GST/company money summaries and month tiles.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin.
TestData: Company: any active; Line: 'Draft item', qty 1, rate 1000; CGST 9; SGST 9.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice, fill the fields per test data.
2. Click Save as draft.
3. Filter the status dropdown to Draft and locate the invoice.
4. Note the invoice total, then compare the GST Summary and company-wise totals with the Draft filter cleared vs applied.
ExpectedResult: Invoice is saved with status Draft. It is not counted in the this-month money tiles nor in receivables (isEligibleInvoice excludes Draft), though it is visible when filtered to Draft.

Name: Cancel an invoice excludes it from outstanding but keeps it in history
Objective: Verify cancelling an invoice via the confirm dialog sets status Cancelled, zeroes its paid/outstanding, and removes it from money summaries while remaining listed.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one Unpaid invoice exists.
Steps:
1. On an Unpaid invoice row, click Cancel invoice.
2. Confirm the danger dialog ('Cancel invoice').
3. Observe the toast and the row status.
4. Check the this-month Outstanding tile and company-wise summary.
ExpectedResult: Status becomes Cancelled; a 'Invoice cancelled' success toast appears; computeInvoice reports paid=0 / outstanding=0 for it; it is excluded from GST/company/month money totals but still visible in the list. Cancelling frees any linked delivery challans and restores deducted stock (invoices, deliveries and stock caches invalidated).

Name: Filters (search, company, status, date range) narrow the list and summaries
Objective: Verify the filter bar filters the invoice grid and that GST/company summaries reflect the filtered rows.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; invoices span multiple companies, statuses and dates.
TestData: A known invoiceNo or reference; a specific company; status Unpaid; a date range covering only some invoices.
Steps:
1. Open /app/invoices.
2. Search by a known invoice number, then clear.
3. Search by a known reference/PO substring, then clear.
4. Select a specific company in the company filter.
5. Set status to Unpaid.
6. Set a from/to date range.
ExpectedResult: The grid, GST Summary tiles and company-wise summary all reflect only rows matching the combined filters (Cancelled always excluded from money totals). Search matches invoiceNo and reference case-insensitively.

Name: Add lines from completed job and from rate list
Objective: Verify the add-from-completed-job and add-from-rate-list helpers append correctly prefilled invoice lines.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; the selected company has a Completed/Delivered job not yet on a line, and at least one active product/rate-list item exists.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice and select the company that owns the completed job.
2. In 'Add from completed job', click the job chip.
3. In '+ Add from rate list…', select a product.
4. Inspect the resulting line rows.
ExpectedResult: A line is added for the job (description = 'partName (partNumber) — jobNo', quantity = completedQty || orderedQty, rate = job.rate ?? 0) and a line for the product (description = product name, quantity 1, rate = product rate). The invoiced job no longer appears in the eligible-jobs list.

Name: Bill directly from received stock imports a stock-deducting line
Objective: Verify selecting a received-stock source in the multi-select adds a line bound to that source with quantity defaulted to available.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; the selected company (or Shop/own) has received stock with available quantity > 0.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice and select the company with available received stock.
2. Open 'Bill directly from received stock' and tick a source.
3. Inspect the added line's description, quantity and the Stock item column.
4. Untick the source and re-inspect the lines.
ExpectedResult: Ticking adds a line with description = material name, quantity = source available, and the Stock item column bound to that source. Unticking removes exactly that line. Only sources for this company or Shop-owned with available>0 are listed.

Name: Delivery-challan picker imports items and marks challans Invoiced on save
Objective: Verify picking Open challans imports their lines (locked from stock re-linking) and, on create, marks the challans as Invoiced against the new invoice.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; the selected company has one or more Open delivery challans.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice and select a company with Open challans.
2. Open 'Add from delivery challans', optionally filter by material, and tick one or more challans.
3. Fill in rates for the imported lines (they import with rate 0) and set date.
4. Click Create invoice.
5. Open the Deliveries module and check the picked challans' status; open the new invoice's DC Ref.
ExpectedResult: Imported lines show 'From challan (already deducted)' in the Stock item column and cannot be re-linked to stock; the DC Ref field auto-fills with the selected DC numbers; on save the challans become status Invoiced linked to the new invoice and stock is not double-deducted.

Name: Edit an existing invoice replaces its lines and recomputes totals
Objective: Verify editing an invoice (not Paid/Cancelled) updates the header and rewrites its lines, and totals recompute.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an editable (Draft/Unpaid/Partially Paid) invoice exists.
TestData: Change one line quantity and adjust discount.
Steps:
1. Click Edit on an Unpaid invoice (note the 'Last updated' timestamp in the modal).
2. Change a line quantity and the discount.
3. Click Save changes.
4. Reopen the invoice (Edit modal) / print view and verify the lines and totals.
ExpectedResult: Success toast ('Invoice updated'); the header updates and its invoice_lines are fully replaced (delete + reinsert) with the new values; totals reflect the change. On reopening the Edit modal the 'Last updated' timestamp has advanced.

Name: Print view and PDF download render invoice with correct totals and DC note
Objective: Verify the print page and generated PDF show shop header, Bill-To, lines, totals split (CGST/SGST), DC-ref note and paid/outstanding.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an invoice with CGST+SGST, a DC reference and at least one payment exists.
Steps:
1. On an invoice row click Print (or navigate to /app/invoices/[id]/print).
2. Verify the on-screen invoice layout, totals split and the DC-ref Note block.
3. Click Download PDF and open the generated file.
ExpectedResult: Print page shows Bill-To, line table, Subtotal, Discount (only when >0), CGST/SGST rows (only when the respective percent is non-zero), Total, and Paid/Outstanding (only when paid>0). The Note block always renders (shows the DC number(s), or '—' when none). The PDF downloads named <invoiceNo>.pdf with amounts formatted 'Rs.' for INR and the DC number(s) in the NOTE block.

Name: Export invoices to Excel reflects current filters
Objective: Verify the Excel export produces a file with the expected columns for the currently filtered rows.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; several invoices exist.
Steps:
1. Open /app/invoices and apply a company filter.
2. Click the Excel button.
3. Open the downloaded workbook.
ExpectedResult: An 'invoices' workbook (sheet 'Invoices') downloads containing only the filtered rows with columns Invoice, Date, Company, Status, Subtotal, CGST, SGST, Total, Paid, Outstanding. Note: the export includes Cancelled rows if they pass the filters (unlike the on-screen money summaries), and CGST/SGST columns are computed without the max(0,...) discount floor.

Name: Line stripping keeps a line if it has a description OR a rate OR a material
Objective: Verify the submit-time line filter keeps a line when it has a non-blank description OR rate>0 OR a materialId, and drops only fully-empty lines.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; New Invoice modal open; a company and date set.
TestData: Line A: description 'Labour', qty 1, rate 0 (kept via description). Line B: description blank, qty 1, rate 50 (kept via rate). Line C: blank description, rate 0, no material (dropped).
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice; select company and date.
2. Add three lines matching Lines A, B and C in the test data.
3. Click Create invoice.
4. Open the created invoice's print view and count the lines.
ExpectedResult: The saved invoice contains Line A and Line B only; the fully-empty Line C is stripped. A rate-only line (blank description) is retained.

Name: createInvoice invokes create_invoice RPC atomically with header and lines
Objective: Verify invoice creation posts to the create_invoice RPC with the correct parameters and returns the created invoice with lines.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; browser dev-tools Network tab open.
Steps:
1. Open Network tab and create a new invoice via the form.
2. Inspect the outbound request to /rest/v1/rpc/create_invoice.
3. Verify the payload includes p_id, p_invoice_no, p_date, p_company_id, p_discount, p_cgst_percent, p_sgst_percent, p_tax_percent, p_status and p_lines[].
4. Confirm the response returns the inserted invoice header.
ExpectedResult: A single create_invoice RPC call inserts header + lines atomically; p_tax_percent equals cgst+sgst; lines carry material_id/source_receipt_id for stock-deducting lines; the invoices and stock query caches are invalidated on success.

Name: setInvoiceStatus RPC on cancel and updateInvoice line-replacement behavior
Objective: Verify cancelling calls set_invoice_status RPC and that updateInvoice deletes then reinserts invoice_lines (only when lines are supplied) rather than patching them, and that the header PATCH ignores the non-column 'lines' field.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; Network tab open; an editable invoice exists.
Steps:
1. Cancel an invoice and inspect the /rest/v1/rpc/set_invoice_status request (p_id, p_status='Cancelled').
2. Edit a different invoice's lines and inspect the invoice_lines DELETE followed by INSERT requests.
3. Confirm the header PATCH does not attempt to write a 'lines' column.
ExpectedResult: Cancel issues set_invoice_status RPC; edit issues a DELETE on invoice_lines by invoice_id then a bulk INSERT of the new rows with line_no ordering; the header update ignores the non-column 'lines' field. Note: the update mutation invalidates only the invoices cache (not stock/deliveries).

Name: Unauthenticated access to /app/invoices and print route is gated
Objective: Verify the authenticated portal gates invoice pages when not logged in.
Precondition: No active session (logged out / cleared storage).
Steps:
1. In a logged-out browser, navigate to /app/invoices.
2. Navigate to /app/invoices/<any-id>/print.
ExpectedResult: The app-shell auth gate (app/app/layout.tsx) blocks access and redirects to login/landing; invoice data is not rendered while unauthenticated.

Name: Over-dispatch guard prevents billing more stock than available
Objective: Verify the client-side per-source over-dispatch guard blocks a new invoice that bills more than a source's available quantity (with the backend RPC as final gate).
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; a received-stock source with a known small available quantity exists for the selected company.
TestData: Source with available = N units; attempt to bill N+ extra units.
Steps:
1. Click New Invoice, select the company, and bill directly from a received-stock source.
2. Set the line quantity above the source's available quantity.
3. Click Create invoice.
ExpectedResult: An error toast states the billing quantity exceeds available for that source and creation is blocked before any RPC is sent. Even if bypassed, the create_invoice RPC rejects the over-dispatch (race-safe final gate).

Name: Invoice lines persist as child rows and rejoin correctly on reload
Objective: Verify invoice_lines are stored as ordered child rows and are correctly joined back to their invoice on listInvoices.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; a multi-line invoice was just created.
Steps:
1. Create a multi-line invoice.
2. Reload /app/invoices and open the invoice's print view.
3. Verify the number, order and values of the lines match what was entered.
ExpectedResult: invoice_lines rows are keyed by invoice_id and returned ordered by line_no; the reloaded invoice shows exactly the entered lines in order with correct qty/rate and amounts.

Name: Editing an invoice does not orphan or duplicate line rows
Objective: Verify the delete-then-reinsert update strategy leaves no stale/duplicate invoice_lines after edits.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; a multi-line editable invoice exists.
TestData: Remove one line and change another line's quantity.
Steps:
1. Edit the invoice: remove one line and change a remaining line's quantity.
2. Save changes.
3. Reload and reopen the invoice; count and verify the lines.
ExpectedResult: The invoice has exactly the remaining lines with updated values; no orphaned old rows and no duplicates; stock allocations for lines with source_receipt_id reflect the edit (source_receipt_id is persisted on reinsert).

Name: Super-admin view renders header, subtitle, footnote and the approved-users table
Objective: Verify /app/roles loads for the super admin with the super-admin copy and a five-column table listing ALL approved users.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one APPROVED user exists in app_state.data.users (approve a registration via /app/approvals if the list is empty).
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/roles.
2. Confirm the PageHeader title 'Roles & Permissions' and subtitle 'Assign roles and choose which modules each approved user can access.'
3. Confirm the footnote (ShieldCheck icon) reads 'Only the super admin can manage roles and module access.'
4. Confirm the table headers read User, Company, Role, Module Access, Actions.
5. Confirm every approved user (regardless of shop or role) appears with name (or '—') + email, company, a Role badge, an access summary and a 'Manage access' button.
ExpectedResult: The page renders with no crash (no <html id="__next_error__">); super-admin subtitle and footnote are shown; the table lists all approved users across every shop.

Name: Admin view renders shop-scoped copy (subtitle and footnote differ from super admin)
Objective: Verify an Admin sees the delegated-manager copy: the shop-scoped subtitle and footnote, distinct from the super-admin strings.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin (me.role === 'Admin', NOT the super admin) whose companyName has at least one approved 'User' teammate.
Steps:
1. As the Admin, navigate to /app/roles.
2. Confirm the page renders (not redirected to /app).
3. Read the PageHeader subtitle.
4. Read the footnote below the card.
ExpectedResult: The subtitle reads 'Grant your shop’s users access to the modules you manage.' and the footnote reads 'You can grant module access to users in your shop. Roles and approvals are handled by the super admin.' — neither matches the super-admin strings.

Name: Empty-state title/description differ between super admin and Admin
Objective: Verify the EmptyState copy is manager-specific when there are no rows to manage.
Precondition: Logged in on the isolated tnt_qa tenant; for the super-admin run no user has status 'approved'; for the Admin run the Admin's shop has zero approved 'User' teammates.
Steps:
1. As the QA super-admin with no approved users, open /app/roles and read the empty state.
2. Then log in as an approved Admin whose shop has no approved User teammates and open /app/roles.
3. Read the empty state for the Admin.
ExpectedResult: Super admin sees UserCog icon, title 'No approved users yet', description 'Approve registrations first — approved users appear here for role and module assignment.'; Admin sees title 'No users in your shop yet', description 'Users who register with your company name and are approved by the super admin will appear here.'; no table headers render in either case.

Name: Role badge tone and access-summary text render per user role/permissions
Objective: Verify the Role badge tone (violet/blue/slate) and Module Access strings ('All modules', 'Dashboard only', 'N of 8 modules') are correct.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; three approved users exist: one Admin, one User with permissions [] (empty), one User with permissions ['production','sales'].
TestData: Admin user; User permissions=[]; User permissions=['production','sales']
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/roles.
2. Inspect the Admin row's Role badge and Module Access cell.
3. Inspect the empty-permissions User row's Module Access cell.
4. Inspect the two-module User row's Module Access cell.
ExpectedResult: Admin row: blue 'Admin' badge and 'All modules'. Empty-permissions User: slate 'User' badge and 'Dashboard only'. Two-module User: slate 'User' badge and '2 of 8 modules'.

Name: Super-admin editor opens with role selector, locked Dashboard row and 8 module checkboxes
Objective: Verify the AccessEditor for the super admin shows the Admin/User role selector plus the locked Dashboard row and all 8 grantable checkboxes.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one approved 'User' exists.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/roles and click 'Manage access' on an approved User row.
2. Confirm the modal title reads 'Manage access — {name or email}'.
3. Confirm the Role section shows both 'Admin' (Full access to every module.) and 'User' (Only the modules selected below.), with 'User' preselected.
4. Confirm the Modules section shows the locked 'Dashboard' row ('Always available') then 8 checkboxes: Production Planning, Inventory, Sales, CRM, Human Resources, Accounts & Finance, Supply Chain, Configuration & Settings.
5. Confirm the Select all/Clear all toggle and the Cancel / Save access footer buttons are present.
ExpectedResult: Modal opens with correct title, both role buttons, the locked Dashboard row, all 8 grantable checkboxes with descriptions, the Select all toggle and Cancel + Save access buttons.

Name: Choosing Admin role hides checkboxes and shows the all-modules note (super admin)
Objective: Verify selecting Admin in the super-admin editor hides the checkbox list, locked Dashboard row and Select all/Clear all toggle and shows the informational note.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least one approved User exists.
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access' for an approved User.
2. Click the 'Admin' role button.
3. Observe the Modules section.
ExpectedResult: The checkbox list, locked Dashboard row and Select all/Clear all toggle disappear; a blue note reads 'Admins have access to all modules — no need to select individually.'

Name: Admin editor HIDES the role selector and shows only the module checkboxes
Objective: Verify that when an Admin opens the editor (canEditRole=false), the Admin/User role selector is not rendered — only the locked Dashboard row and grantable module checkboxes appear.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin whose shop has at least one approved 'User' teammate.
Steps:
1. As the Admin, navigate to /app/roles and click 'Manage access' on a teammate User row.
2. Confirm the modal title 'Manage access — {name or email}'.
3. Look for the Role section (the Admin/User two-button selector).
4. Inspect the Modules section.
ExpectedResult: No Role selector is shown (no Admin/User buttons); the editor shows the locked Dashboard 'Always available' row, the 8 grantable module checkboxes and the Select all/Clear all toggle; Save access and Cancel are present.

Name: Editor pre-populates checked modules from the user's existing permissions
Objective: Verify the AccessEditor initializes its checked set from user.permissions filtered to valid module keys the manager is allowed to grant.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User with role 'User' and permissions ['inventory','crm'].
TestData: permissions=['inventory','crm']
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/roles and click 'Manage access' for that User.
2. Inspect the preselected role and which module checkboxes are checked.
ExpectedResult: 'User' role is preselected; exactly Inventory and CRM checkboxes are checked, all others unchecked; the Dashboard row stays locked/always-on.

Name: Invalid/unknown permission keys are ignored when populating the editor
Objective: Verify isModuleKey filtering drops stale/unknown keys and 'dashboard' (always-on) so the editor only checks recognised grantable modules.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User whose permissions = ['sales','legacy_module','dashboard'].
TestData: permissions=['sales','legacy_module','dashboard']
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access' for that User.
2. Inspect the checked module checkboxes.
3. Note that 'dashboard' is the locked always-on row (not a checkbox) and 'legacy_module' is not a real module.
ExpectedResult: Only the 'Sales' checkbox is checked; 'legacy_module' and 'dashboard' produce no checkbox; no crash.

Name: Admin list membership is case/whitespace-insensitive on company name (sameCompany)
Objective: Verify sameCompany trims and lowercases both sides so a User whose companyName differs from the Admin's only by case/spacing is still listed, while a truly different company is not.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin with companyName e.g. 'Acme Tools'; three approved Users exist: one companyName '  acme tools ' (case+space variant), one 'Acme Tools' exact, one 'Beta Works' (different company). All have role 'User'.
TestData: Admin company 'Acme Tools'; Users: '  acme tools ', 'Acme Tools', 'Beta Works'
Steps:
1. As the Admin, navigate to /app/roles.
2. Inspect which User rows are listed.
ExpectedResult: The '  acme tools ' and 'Acme Tools' Users are both listed (matched after trim+lowercase); the 'Beta Works' User is NOT listed.

Name: Super admin promotes a User to Admin — persists role Admin with empty permissions and grants all modules
Objective: Verify saving the Admin role persists role 'Admin' and permissions [], refreshes the table to 'All modules', and unlocks every module for that user.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User with a limited module set exists, with known login credentials.
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access' for the User, click 'Admin', click 'Save access'.
2. Confirm the success toast 'Access updated for {name or email}' and that the modal closes.
3. Confirm the row now shows a blue 'Admin' badge and Module Access 'All modules'.
4. Sign out and log in as that user (or evaluate effectiveModuleKeys) and confirm every module is reachable.
ExpectedResult: The user is saved as role 'Admin' with permissions [] in app_state; the table shows blue Admin / 'All modules'; when the user signs in, filterGroupsByAccess returns all NAV_GROUPS so every module is available.

Name: Admin grants a shop User a subset of modules — sidebar filters and blocked routes redirect
Objective: Verify an Admin (no role selector) can grant a teammate User specific modules, the keys persist, and on that user's session the sidebar filters while an ungranted module URL redirects to /app.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin whose shop has an approved 'User' teammate with known login credentials.
TestData: Grant only Inventory + Sales
Steps:
1. As the Admin, open 'Manage access' for the teammate User (note there is no role selector), check only 'Inventory' and 'Sales', click 'Save access'.
2. Confirm the success toast and Module Access now reads '2 of 8 modules'.
3. Sign out and log in as that teammate User.
4. Confirm the sidebar shows Dashboard, Inventory and Sales only.
5. Manually enter an ungranted module URL such as /app/hrm.
ExpectedResult: permissions saved as ['inventory','sales']; the user's sidebar lists only Dashboard/Inventory/Sales; navigating to /app/hrm triggers the route guard which router.replace('/app').

Name: Out-of-scope modules the user already had are PRESERVED on an Admin save
Objective: Verify the `preserved` merge in onSave keeps any of the user's existing modules that fall outside the manager's allowedKeys, so a scoped manager cannot strip access another manager granted.
Precondition: Logged in as a manager whose allowedKeys is a RESTRICTED subset (e.g. a future Admin allowed only ['inventory','sales']); a teammate 'User' already has permissions ['inventory','hrm','accounts'] where hrm and accounts are OUTSIDE the manager's allowedKeys. (If no restricted Admin fixture is available, verify the same preserve logic via a code/behaviour review of onSave's `preserved` filter.)
TestData: manager allowedKeys=['inventory','sales']; user permissions=['inventory','hrm','accounts']
Steps:
1. As the scoped manager, open 'Manage access' for that User — confirm only the grantable (in-scope) modules render as checkboxes and the pre-checked set is limited to in-scope keys (e.g. only Inventory).
2. Uncheck Inventory and check Sales, then click 'Save access'.
3. Have the super admin reopen 'Manage access' for the same user (or inspect app_state.data.users) to read the full persisted permissions.
ExpectedResult: Persisted permissions become the union of preserved out-of-scope keys and the newly chosen in-scope keys — ['hrm','accounts','sales'] (order-independent). The out-of-scope 'hrm' and 'accounts' the scoped manager could not see were NOT removed; only the in-scope Inventory→Sales change applied.

Name: Select all then Clear all toggles every grantable checkbox
Objective: Verify the Select all / Clear all toggle checks all grantable modules then clears them and the label flips, without affecting the locked Dashboard row.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User with partial or no modules checked (super admin has all 8 grantable).
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access' for a User, keep role 'User'.
2. Click 'Select all'.
3. Confirm all 8 grantable checkboxes become checked and the toggle now reads 'Clear all'.
4. Click 'Clear all'.
5. Confirm all 8 uncheck and the toggle reverts to 'Select all'.
ExpectedResult: 'Select all' checks every grantable module (label→'Clear all'); 'Clear all' unchecks them (label→'Select all'); the locked Dashboard row is unaffected throughout.

Name: Legacy User with permissions == null defaults to full access (not locked out)
Objective: Verify a User whose permissions is unset/null is treated as 'all' by effectiveModuleKeys, so the table reads 'All modules' and the user is not locked out.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User whose app_state record has NO permissions key (undefined/null).
TestData: permissions = undefined
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/roles and read the legacy User's Module Access cell.
2. Sign in as that user (or evaluate effectiveModuleKeys) and inspect the sidebar.
ExpectedResult: Module Access reads 'All modules'; when the user signs in every module is available and no route-guard redirect fires (permissions == null ⇒ 'all').

Name: Cancel discards edits without persisting
Objective: Verify closing the editor via Cancel does not call updateUserAccess and leaves the user's role/permissions unchanged.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User with a known module set exists.
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access' and note the current access summary.
2. Toggle several checkboxes and/or switch the role.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
4. Reopen 'Manage access' for the same user.
ExpectedResult: No success toast; the table access summary is unchanged; reopening shows the original role and checked modules (no write occurred).

Name: Save access issues an app_state upsert and invalidates the users query
Objective: Verify Save performs a read-modify-write on app_state (singleton) and onSuccess invalidates qk.users.all so the table refreshes without reload.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; DevTools Network open; an approved User exists.
Steps:
1. Open DevTools Network and filter for app_state / rest requests.
2. Open 'Manage access', change the module selection, click 'Save access'.
3. Observe a select on app_state then an upsert (POST/PATCH) writing the merged users JSON.
4. Confirm the table Module Access cell updates in place without a full reload.
ExpectedResult: A select of app_state (id=singleton) followed by an upsert (2xx) containing the merged users array; onSuccess invalidates qk.users.all and the row's access summary refreshes automatically.

Name: Save failure surfaces an error toast and keeps the modal open
Objective: Verify that when updateUserAccess rejects (RLS denial, network failure), the UI shows the error toast and keeps the editor open with edits intact.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; ability to force a failure (block the app_state upsert in DevTools, or go offline).
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access' and change the selection.
2. Force the upsert to fail (block the request or disable network).
3. Click 'Save access'.
ExpectedResult: An error toast 'Could not update access' (or a more specific toUserMessage) appears; the modal stays open with edits intact; no success toast; the table row is unchanged.

Name: Roles nav item is visible to an Admin (manageAccess flag)
Objective: Verify the '/app/roles' nav item now carries manageAccess:true so it renders for an Admin as well as the super admin (delegation entry point).
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin (me.role === 'Admin', NOT super admin).
Steps:
1. As the Admin, open the Configuration & Settings group in the sidebar.
2. Look for the 'Roles & Permissions' link (/app/roles).
3. Click it and confirm it opens the page.
ExpectedResult: The 'Roles & Permissions' link IS present for the Admin (canManageAccess true) and opens /app/roles; the super-admin-only 'User Approvals' (/app/approvals, superAdmin:true) is NOT shown to the Admin.

Name: Roles nav item is hidden from a plain User
Objective: Verify the manageAccess-flagged Roles link does NOT render for a regular User (canManageAccess false), matching the page-level canManage guard.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved 'User' (me.role === 'User', not Admin, not super admin).
Steps:
1. As the User, inspect the sidebar (and the Configuration & Settings group if visible).
2. Confirm there is no 'Roles & Permissions' link.
3. Attempt to reach /app/roles directly via the address bar.
ExpectedResult: No Roles & Permissions link appears for the plain User; a direct visit to /app/roles is redirected to /app (page-level guard). NOTE: this replaces the outdated 'Roles nav item hidden from ALL non-super-admins' case — Admins now DO see it.

Name: Page-level guard redirects a plain User away from /app/roles
Objective: Verify a user where canManage is false (a plain 'User') who navigates to /app/roles is redirected to /app and never sees the roles UI.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved 'User' (NOT Admin, NOT super admin).
Steps:
1. As the User, enter /app/roles directly in the address bar.
2. Observe the resulting page and URL.
ExpectedResult: RolesPage returns null and the guard effect navigates to /app; the roles table, headers and 'Manage access' controls are never displayed to a plain User.

Name: An Admin cannot escalate a shop User to Admin (no role selector, no role change)
Objective: Verify an Admin can never promote a User: the editor omits the role selector (canEditRole=false) and any save keeps role 'User'.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin with an approved 'User' teammate.
Steps:
1. As the Admin, open 'Manage access' for the teammate User.
2. Confirm no Admin/User role selector is rendered.
3. Change some module checkboxes and click 'Save access'.
4. Reopen the row (or have the super admin inspect it) to confirm the user's role.
ExpectedResult: There is no way for the Admin to choose 'Admin'; the save persists role 'User' (onSave receives role 'User' since the editor's role state can never leave 'User' without the hidden selector); the teammate remains a 'User'.

Name: Admin list never includes other shops, other Admins or the super admin
Objective: Verify an Admin's managed list is strictly scoped: only approved role-'User' accounts in the same company, excluding themselves, other Admins, other shops' users and the super admin.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved Admin (company 'Acme Tools'); fixtures exist: an approved User in 'Acme Tools', an approved User in 'Beta Works', a second approved Admin in 'Acme Tools', and the super-admin account.
Steps:
1. As the Admin, navigate to /app/roles.
2. Enumerate the rows shown in the table.
ExpectedResult: Only the same-company approved 'User' appears; the Beta Works user, the other Acme Admin, the super admin and the Admin's own row are all excluded.

Name: Client-side module gating is UX-only — RLS still protects data server-side
Objective: Verify module keys and the app_state RLS policy are the real guard: a hand-crafted write or read that bypasses the client cannot escalate access or persist an unauthorised role/permission change.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved non-super-admin (Admin or limited User) with DevTools; know a user id in app_state.data.users and that a second tenant's data exists (tnt_qa isolation).
Steps:
1. As the limited user, confirm the route guard redirects ungranted module URLs to /app.
2. In DevTools, attempt a direct Supabase upsert to app_state (id=singleton) mutating another user's role/permissions.
3. Also attempt a direct REST read of a table behind an ungranted module or another tenant's rows.
4. Observe the server responses.
ExpectedResult: The app_state upsert is rejected by RLS (no persisted change) and cross-scope reads return no unauthorised rows (is_app_approved()+tenant_id enforced server-side) — proving module keys and the delegation UI never grant real data access.

Name: Saved role and permissions persist in app_state.data.users across reload
Objective: Verify a saved role/permissions change is durably written into app_state.data.users and survives a full reload/re-query.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User exists.
TestData: role 'User' with permissions ['accounts','configuration']
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access', keep role 'User', check only 'Accounts & Finance' and 'Configuration & Settings', click 'Save access'.
2. Confirm the success toast and Module Access '2 of 8 modules'.
3. Hard-refresh /app/roles.
4. Reopen 'Manage access' for the same user.
ExpectedResult: After reload permissions still read ['accounts','configuration'] (both checked, role 'User'); the write persisted in app_state.data.users.

Name: Admin role persists permissions as an empty array (overwrites prior key list)
Objective: Verify saving the Admin role writes permissions:[] so a later switch back to User starts from zero checked modules.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; an approved User currently granted several modules (e.g. ['production','sales','crm']).
Steps:
1. Open 'Manage access', switch role to 'Admin', click 'Save access'.
2. Confirm the row shows Admin / 'All modules'.
3. Reopen 'Manage access', switch back to 'User', inspect the checkboxes.
ExpectedResult: After the Admin save permissions is stored as []; reopening and switching to User shows NO checkboxes checked (the prior ['production','sales','crm'] was overwritten).

Name: updateUserAccess updates only the target user in the users JSON array (no collateral writes)
Objective: Verify the read-modify-write in updateUserAccess merges the patch onto the findIndex-matched user only and preserves every other user's fields.
Precondition: Logged in as QA super-admin; at least three approved users exist with distinct roles/permissions.
Steps:
1. Record the role and permissions of two non-target users.
2. Open 'Manage access' for the third (target) user, change its module selection, click 'Save access'.
3. Hard-refresh and reopen the two non-target users' editors (or inspect app_state.data.users).
ExpectedResult: Only the target user's role/permissions changed; the two other users' role and permissions are exactly as before (the upsert rewrites the whole users array but merges the patch onto the single matched index).

Name: Vendors list renders with all columns and status badges
Objective: Verify the vendors list page renders the header, search box, and table with Code, Name, GSTIN, Phone, Status, Actions columns and correct Active/Inactive badges.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved user (QA super-admin); at least one active and one inactive vendor exist in the current tenant.
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/vendors.
2. Observe the page header 'Vendors' with subtitle 'Suppliers and subcontractors used by purchases and job work' and the 'Add Vendor' button.
3. Observe the search input with placeholder 'Search name, code, GSTIN…'.
4. Inspect the table header row and both an active-vendor and an inactive-vendor data row.
ExpectedResult: Table shows columns Code (monospace), Name, GSTIN, Phone, Status, Actions. Empty GSTIN/Phone render as '—'. Active vendors show a green 'Active' badge; inactive vendors show a gray 'Inactive' badge. Each row has Edit (pencil) and Delete (trash) icon buttons; rows are ordered alphabetically by name.

Name: Loading skeleton and empty state display correctly
Objective: Verify the TableSkeleton shows while loading and the EmptyState shows both when no vendors exist and when a search matches nothing (same UI branch).
Precondition: Logged in as an approved user (QA super-admin).
TestData: Search term unlikely to match, e.g. 'zzzznomatch'
Steps:
1. Navigate to /app/vendors and observe the initial state before data resolves (throttle network if needed).
2. Once loaded, type 'zzzznomatch' into the search box.
3. Clear the search box.
ExpectedResult: During load a table skeleton (8 rows x 5 cols) is shown. When no rows match the search, the EmptyState with the building icon, title 'No vendors' and description 'Add a supplier or subcontractor to use in purchases and job work.' is shown in place of the table (note: this is the same branch used when the tenant genuinely has no vendors). Clearing the search restores the list.

Name: Add/Edit modal renders all fields and edit metadata
Objective: Verify the VendorForm modal shows all input fields, autofocuses Name, and in edit mode shows the vendor code in the title and the last-updated timestamp.
Precondition: Logged in as an approved user (QA super-admin); at least one vendor exists.
Steps:
1. Click 'Add Vendor' and inspect the modal title, fields, focus, and footer buttons.
2. Cancel the modal, then click the Edit (pencil) icon on an existing vendor row.
3. Inspect the edit modal title, the 'Last updated' line, footer button, and that fields are prefilled.
ExpectedResult: Add modal titled 'Add Vendor' with fields: Vendor Name (required, autofocused), GSTIN, Phone, Email, Status select (Active/Inactive), Address textarea, Notes textarea, and Cancel / 'Add vendor' buttons. Edit modal titled 'Edit VENxxx' shows a right-aligned 'Last updated <datetime>' line and a 'Save changes' button; all fields are prefilled with the vendor's stored values.

Name: Create a new vendor with auto-generated code
